reason: The cited evidence supports that nanohierarchical structures and nanocrystalline glaze layers can reduce wear and friction in some alloys, but it does not provide any evidence that the proposed laser shock peening plus heat pulse treatment can create such a layer in CoCrFeMnNi, nor that the layer would dynamically reorganize into a stable glaze under the specified conditions.
premises: Nanohierarchical/heterogeneous microstructures can yield ultralow wear across a wide temperature range in complex alloys
At high temperatures, a dense nanocrystalline glaze layer can form via tribo-oxidation and provide solid lubrication
Ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layers in CoCrFeMnNi can produce low friction (~0.3) and low wear in inert environments
Laser shock peening combined with a heat pulse can pre-engineer an ultra-nanocrystalline, nanohierarchical surface layer in CoCrFeMnNi
The pre-engineered layer will dynamically reorganize into a stable self-lubricating glaze during sliding
